newsitem.title: UK: National Power drops as profits disappoint.
newsitem.headline: National Power drops as profits disappoint.

text.p: Shares in National Power Plc dropped in pre-market trading on Wednesday after lower-than-expected profits for the year ended March 31 1997.
The stock was down 15p at 547-1/2 by 0703 GMT while rival PowerGen Plc, which reports on Thursday, was down 5p at 692-1/2.

National Power posted a drop in pre-tax profit to 740 million stg, before an exceptional charge of 22 million stg, compared with analyst expectations mostly in a range between 760 million stg and 792 million.
The dividend was raised nine percent to 25.0p.
"The profits were a bit light...and the dividend increase was a bit thin," said Nigel Hawkins, analyst at Yamaichi. "The concern, particularly on the UK, is that the best is in the past."
Today's decline in National Power shares came after they reached a 13-month high of 582p on May 16.
National Power said it had been a "satisfactory year" despite a drop in earnings which reflected the increasingly competitive nature of the UK market.
The company said trading in the early part of the year was in line with its expectations, and said it expected competitive pressures in the UK business to intensify.
It said it would consider allowing dividend cover to shrink in order to preserve dividend growth.
